claims.statement: The current consolidated Polish Public Procurement Law requires public construction contracts to specify contractor-payment rules conditioned on evidence that due subcontractor and further-subcontractor remuneration was paid.

Article 465 requires direct payment only for eligible accepted or submitted subcontract arrangements after nonpayment, with contractor comment, possible denial or court deposit and fact-specific proof of entitlement.

GDDKiA identifies unreadable copies, inconsistent contract and invoice references, missing evidence, unauthorized signatures, late amendments and unregistered subcontract arrangements as causes that block or delay payment requests.
For its 2014-2020 programme, GDDKiA reported more than 1,800 accepted direct-payment cases worth over 562m PLN and nearly 1,100 further applications leading contractors to pay over 353m PLN.
Polish procurement under the Public Procurement Law reached about 330.4bn PLN in 2024, with construction works representing 39% of awarded value.

The free government PEF platform already supports structured public-procurement invoices and related documents through web tools and API, although internal approval workflows remain in each authority's systems.

PlanRadar, PROGPOL and Archdesk already cover document control, approvals, subcontractor records, acceptance protocols, invoices and construction payment workflows, with PlanRadar listing plans from EUR 26 to EUR 129 per internal user monthly.
GDDKiA treats contractor and subcontractor employee data as GDPR-governed project data and recognizes IT processors, access rights, correction and retention obligations.

contrary_evidence: PEF is a free government channel for structured invoices and related public-procurement documents, reducing the value of a generic submission portal.
PlanRadar, Archdesk and Polish PROGPOL already offer document control, approvals, subcontractor records and invoice-to-acceptance workflows.
Article 465 entitlement is fact-specific and includes contractor objections, denial and court-deposit branches that cannot be safely reduced to an automated ready/not-ready legal answer.

PlanRadar's published EUR 26-129 per-user monthly pricing challenges the original 1,500-7,000 PLN per-project monthly range unless the Polish payment-proof specialization creates measurable incremental value.
GDDKiA's large direct-payment figures validate the problem but are historical, road-program-specific and include contractor financial failure, not only document defects.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with one permissioned renewable/electrical public-works project through the founder's family-business access and sell the checklist configuration to the main contractor or administrator; adviser and contract-administrator referrals remain an unvalidated second channel.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast: 150 concurrent projects at 4,000 PLN monthly would yield 7.2m PLN ARR. At 22% EBITDA, a 4x operating-value multiple and 80% founder ownership, equity could be about 5.1m PLN in years 7-10; reaching that scale requires repeatable configuration and distribution and must not double-count retained cash.
economics.founder_time: 15-23 hours weekly for one narrowly templated pilot, near the part-time ceiling during mobilization; a procurement lawyer or contract specialist must own legal interpretation and template approval.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 50-70% during service-heavy pilots, potentially 72-84% after reusable authority templates, integrations and self-service participant onboarding; no observed delivery-cost data exist.
economics.payback: Unknown. Target 6-12 months after a paid pilot because configuration and stakeholder onboarding are substantial and public-authority sales can be much longer; family access reduces discovery cost but does not prove external acquisition.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated wedge hypothesis: 5,000-15,000 PLN setup plus 1,500-4,000 PLN per active project monthly. The premium over low-seat-count PlanRadar requires measured prevention of a payment hold or administrator labor saving.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Payment draws and subcontractor evidence recur during a multi-year project, but revenue ends at project close and can migrate into the contractor's ERP; repeat depends on carrying templates and relationships to the next project.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned authority-template mappings and labeled rejection/cure patterns connect contracts, amendments, acceptances, invoices and downstream-payment evidence, if customers allow de-identified reuse.
fingerprint.customer: Polish SME main contractors and contract administrators on public construction projects, initially renewable and electrical packages with multiple subcontractors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A permissioned family-business pilot proves one template, then procurement advisers and contract administrators introduce the adapter at project mobilization; PEF/KSeF and existing ERP/DMS systems remain systems of record.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Project-specific payment-evidence graph and completeness adapter with paid setup, recurring project fee and optional document-control service; it links existing records and never decides legal entitlement.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The main contractor or contract administrator pays per active project when a draw receives a source-linked completeness view and exceptions are routed before submission.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A public-works payment draw or subcontractor request is approaching, but accepted contract, amendment, work acceptance, invoice, authorization or downstream-payment evidence is missing, inconsistent or stored across systems.

founder_fit: The founder's renewable-installation family access can supply a lawful permissioned design environment, but it is not external market validation.
Evidence graphs, extraction and anomaly rules match data-science strengths and can be prototyped within 60,000 PLN.
A one-project pilot can fit the founder's part-time limit if legal interpretation and high-touch document control are delegated.
The model avoids camera-based distribution but requires trust with contractors, administrators and advisers.
risks: A completeness label may prejudice a claim if users mistake it for a legal entitlement decision; outputs must remain source-linked administrative checks approved by counsel.
Contracting-authority, FIDIC and project-specific templates may vary enough to make configuration a consultancy rather than scalable SaaS.
Main contractors and subcontractors may not share prices, bank confirmations, amendments or dispute facts in one workspace.
PEF, KSeF, incumbent construction ERPs and document systems can absorb or commoditize the feature.
Personal and commercially sensitive records require strict role permissions, processing agreements, retention controls and audit logs.
Family-pilot convenience may hide weak external willingness to pay and long procurement cycles.
Project-level churn and service-heavy onboarding can prevent the assumed margins and scale.

structure.commercial_archetype: Project payment-gate adapter layered on public-works systems of record
structure.control_point: The source-linked administrative completeness review immediately before a contractor draw or subcontractor request is submitted
structure.critical_dependency: Authorized participants must supply authoritative project records and a qualified specialist must approve project-specific rules without the software claiming legal entitlement.

thesis: Create a narrow payment-evidence graph for Polish public construction, initially one renewable or electrical subcontracting project. It links accepted subcontracts and amendments, authorized acceptance records, invoices and downstream-payment proof from existing PEF/KSeF, ERP and document systems, then exposes missing or inconsistent links before a draw. GDDKiA's published failure modes show real administrative pain, but free government infrastructure and broad incumbents make a generic portal unattractive. The defensible wedge is authority-specific evidence mapping and auditability, not document storage, and every rule set must be approved by a qualified specialist because the software neither decides entitlement nor represents a party.
title: Public-Works Payment Evidence Adapter
uncertainties: Frequency, delay days and cash value of payment holds caused primarily by remediable evidence gaps
Whether main contractor, administrator or subcontractor owns budget and will pay the proposed project fee
External willingness to pay beyond a family-access pilot
Template variation across authorities, projects and contract forms and the hours required per configuration
Whether project participants will share pricing, bank and dispute records with appropriately scoped permissions
Integration feasibility with PEF, KSeF and the initial contractor's ERP/document stack
Measured reduction in administrator labor, rejected draws or days to payment
Project-to-project renewal, partner referral rate, sales cycle and mature gross margin
Whether de-identified cure-pattern reuse is contractually permitted
